subject: Segregated control plane & custodian roles for private deployment
messages:
From: Danielle Park <dpark@medbridge-ai.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Private deploy - control plane / key custody questions

Hi Avery,

Thanks for walking us through the Private deployment options yesterday. Legal and our infra team had a few follow-ups before we sign the amendment:

1) Customer-held keys: can you confirm whether Redwood requires any escrow or split-key escrow for on-prem installs, or if we can retain sole custody with a non-exportable HSM under our control?

2) Operator access: in your diagram you mentioned an "operator" role that performs maintenance. Who technically has the ability to decrypt traffic or access model KV, and can that be limited to a local, customer-side admin?

3) Subprocessors: we expect a third-party integrator to perform initial rack and install in our EU colo. Can you provide a list of subprocessors that would be present on-prem or have network-level access during install?

We need concise answers so Legal (EMEA) can review the DPA changes.

Appreciate it — Danielle
Danielle Park
Head of Infrastructure
MedBridge AI

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Park <dpark@medbridge-ai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy - control plane / key custody questions

Hi Danielle — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by detail and an attachment with an operator-access matrix.

1) Customer-held keys: You can retain sole custody. For our Private offering we support customer-managed KMS/HSM (bring-your-own-key). We do not require key escrow by default. Where customers request a managed break-glass option we can include an escrow protocol, but that is strictly optional and documented in the amendment.

2) Operator access: By default the Redwood control plane is logically separated from the data plane in Private deployments. Operator accounts in our Ops org do not receive decryption keys. Local admins (customer-provided) hold the keys and manage node boot. Redwood support staff can be provisioned only with ephemeral, least-privilege access tokens for diagnostics that cannot decrypt model KV or persisted user data.

3) Subprocessors: For installs we rely on two partner roles: (a) certified field integrators (on-site engineers) and (b) a remote telemetry relay service (EU-only) that carries anonymized health metrics. Neither has access to customer keys or decrypted data. See the attached operator-access-matrix.pdf for exact capabilities.

I'll highlight the clauses Legal will want: explicit language that (i) keys remain customer property and are not escrowed without explicit request, (ii) operator accounts are role-separated and cannot access plaintext data, and (iii) subprocessors are limited to install/telemetry and listed by name in the amendment. Monica and Karthik — flag anything I missed for the DPA draft.

Best,
Avery
Avery Johnson
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-13T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy - control plane / key custody questions

Avery / team — adding legal-ops details we typically propose for EU customers. These are recommended edits to the DPA language (I'll attach a draft docx in the next email):

• Key ownership clause: "Customer retains sole ownership and control of cryptographic keys used for data encryption and model KV. Redwood shall not have the ability to derive or reconstruct keys; any temporary support mechanisms must be initiated by Customer-approved workflows."

• Escrow opt-in: "Break-glass or escrow mechanisms are available only by Customer opt-in; such mechanisms require documented dual-approval, time-limited access tokens, and audit trail export to Customer's SIEM."

• Subprocessor scope: list field integrators (names redacted until customer's procurement sign-off) and the telemetry relay; subprocessors shall have no key access and must be bound by contract clauses matching DPA obligations.

• Auditing: provide sample audit-log format and frequency; include the audit-log-sample.csv as an example export that shows which operator actions are recorded and what is redacted.

We should also offer an operational playbook session with their infra team so they see the boot flow and key handoff. Karthik — can you prepare 20–30 minute tech runbook?

—Monica
Monica Patel
Director, Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Legal EMEA <legal-emea@clientco.eu>

Subject: Re: Private deploy - control plane / key custody questions

Good morning,

Thank you for the clarifications. A couple of specific follow-ups from the legal review:

1) Transfers: can you confirm whether any telemetry or operational metadata will be transferred outside the EU during normal operations or only under explicit opt-in? We need the DPA to state that no operational metadata leaves the EU except for those anonymized health metrics and only if customer configures global relay.

2) Emergency access: what is the exact process for a break-glass request, and will that process require a court order or can Redwood self-initiate under Incident Response? We prefer a model where customer consent or a mutually agreed emergency workflow is required.

3) Subprocessors list: we will need named entities and their contract dates for any integrators with site access. Can you provide a redacted list now and unredacted once procurement checks are complete?

Please respond with the proposed amendment language and the operational playbook link.

Regards,
Legal EMEA

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Park <dpark@medbridge-ai.com>, Legal EMEA <legal-emea@clientco.eu>

Date: 2026-10-15T16:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy - control plane / key custody questions

Hi Danielle / Legal EMEA — thanks for the precise asks. Quick responses and next steps below, attached draft amendment and a link to a short runbook session we can run this week.

1) Telemetry / transfers: By default all telemetry endpoints for EU Private deployments are routed to our EU telemetry relay and stored in-region. No operational metadata is sent outside the EU unless the Customer explicitly enables a global relay in the configuration UI. We'll add the following sentence to the DPA amendment: "Operational telemetry and health metrics for EU Private deployments will be retained within the EU and will not be transferred outside the EU unless the Customer enables global relay functionality."

2) Break-glass: Our break-glass process is strictly customer-controlled. Redwood may only initiate temporary elevated access under a Customer-approved emergency workflow documented in the amendment; such access requires dual approval (Redwood on-call lead + Customer security approver), is time-limited, fully audited, and exports an immutable record to the Customer's SIEM. Redwood will not self-initiate based solely on Incident Response protocols. We'll propose language to that effect.

3) Subprocessors: Attached is a redacted list of approved field integrators and the telemetry provider. Once procurement completes an NDA, we will provide unredacted details and contract dates.

Action items: 
• I attached proposed-dpa-amendment-draft.docx with the clauses above.
• Proposed 30-minute runbook: Tue 2026-10-20 09:00 BST (we can revise).
• DocuSign amendment: I'll create and share a link after we receive a confirmation that procurement is comfortable with the redacted integrator list.

Let us know if you want to include an explicit KMS HSM vendor whitelist (we can add it as an annex).

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
